_readme: Social vulnerability index per Census 2011 unit (audit M12, Phase 2). Built by tools/build_svi.py; do not edit by hand.

indicators.illiteracy7plus: Illiteracy, age 7+: education limits access to warnings, recovery information and formal jobs (a core social vulnerability variable, Cutter et al. 2003).
indicators.children0to6: Children aged 0-6: dependants who need help to evacuate and are most at risk from floodwater-borne disease.
indicators.casualWorkerShare: Casual (marginal) workers among workers: under six months' work a year, so the least income security; flood days cost them wages.

method: Mean of the three indicators' z-scores across the four units (equal weights). Class higher if > +0.5, lower if < -0.5, else middle. The classes rank the four units against each other; they are not absolute levels.
note: Town-level, not ward-level: ward tables exist for Panaji but no open ward boundaries, so every cell in Panaji (M Corp. + OG) gets one class. Unit boundaries are DataMeet's 2001 village/town polygons, which are approximate. Bambolim's census population is male-heavy (about 70% male), probably an institutional population, which lowers its children and casual-worker shares. Cells outside these four units (Curca and slivers of other villages, about 1,600 GHS-POP people) are 'not classified'.
